The prevalence of visible fungi growth and damp was high in flats, with 40% reporting visible fungi and 30% reporting dampness.
visible fungi growth and damp conditions assessed using a questionnaire were not associated with airborne fungi, ( 1 → 3)-β-D- glucan and fungal spores.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between visible fungi growth in flats, airborne fungi and the presence of (1→3) -β-D-glucans.
the relationship between dampness in flats and the indoor air quality.
the development of an effective, non-invasive method for the assessment of fungal contamination of building materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the questionnaire-based method is not a suitable tool for the detection of dampness and fungi growth in flats.
there is a strong association between visible fungi growth in flats and the concentrations of fungi, (1-3)-β-D glucan and fungal spores in the air.
there is not enough evidence to support or refute the hypothesis that dampness and visible mould in homes is related to adverse health effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a number of factors are associated with fungal spores, (1→ 3)-β-D-Glucan and fungal growth in flats.
the questionnaire is a valuable instrument in the assessment of dampness and visible fungi growth.

the presence of visible fungi development was connected with higher concentrations of airborne fungi and fungal spores, and higher (1→3)β-D-glucans concentrations in the indoor atmosphere, and dampness in flats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of visible mold and dampness in the indoor environment can be a useful indicator of the presence of airborne fungal spores, (1→ 3)-β-D-Glucan, and fungal DNA.
the current approach for assessing the impact of indoor dampness and mold on health is flawed and needs to be revised.
